pages.quiz:
GEOGRAPHY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: GEOGRAPHY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Introduction to Geography is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Introduction to Geography with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Introduction to Geography.
   C. Say Introduction to Geography never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Introduction to Geography as rumours only.

2. Which statement about Agriculture is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Agriculture never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Agriculture.
   C. Treat Agriculture as rumours only.
   D. Explain Agriculture with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

3. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Avoiding all community work
   B. Littering in markets
   C. Destroying road signs
   D. Obeying laws and caring for public property

4. Which statement about Geographic Information Systems is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Geographic Information Systems never happens in Kenya.
   B. Explain Geographic Information Systems with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Treat Geographic Information Systems as rumours only.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Geographic Information Systems.

5. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Measure rainfall only
   B. Name the president
   C. Replace the compass rose
   D. Explain symbols used on a map

6. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Hide all money underground
   B. Avoid saving forever
   C. Ignore prices in shops
   D. Plan income and spending wisely

7. Which statement about Vulcanicity is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Vulcanicity with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Vulcanicity.
   C. Say Vulcanicity never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Vulcanicity as rumours only.

8. Which statement about Rocks is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Explain Rocks with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Rocks.
   C. Say Rocks never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Rocks as rumours only.

9. Which statement about Industry is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Industry as rumours only.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Industry.
   C. Explain Industry with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Say Industry never happens in Kenya.

10. Which statement about Earthquakes is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Earthquakes never happens in Kenya.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Earthquakes.
   C. Treat Earthquakes as rumours only.
   D. Explain Earthquakes with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

11. Which statement about Folding is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Folding.
   B. Explain Folding with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   C. Treat Folding as rumours only.
   D. Say Folding never happens in Kenya.

12. Which statement about Statistical Methods is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Statistical Methods.
   B. Say Statistical Methods never happens in Kenya.
   C. Treat Statistical Methods as rumours only.
   D. Explain Statistical Methods with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Geographic Information Systems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Rocks and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Folding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Vulcanicity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
